A1.justification: Both 11-page PDFs describe the same ARMFlow/ReMFlow study, with readable text, equations, figures, and tables. Inspection through the final references establishes that neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original reaction-generation experiments on InterHuman and InterX, including quantitative comparisons, ablations, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: Section 5 retains these original experiments and additionally reports R2R baseline results on both datasets.

M1.justification: The CNN-VAE, offline ReMFlow, causal context encoder and MLP predictor in ARMFlow, MeanFlow objectives, and BSCE procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 retains the same steps.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate text-conditioned online and offline human reaction generation on InterHuman and InterX. The added baseline uses existing coverage; no dataset, task, or distinct test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Ready-to-React (R2R) to the online comparison on both datasets, alongside InterFormer, CAMDM, and ReGenNet. The offline and ablation comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Reported metrics, motion representations, training budgets, model sizes, CFG strengths, and CAMDM initialization and context-window settings are unchanged. No separate new evaluation protocol is specified for the added R2R rows.

E4.justification: Tables 4-6 retain the same diffusion/flow objective ablations and GTE, rollout, and BSCE training comparisons. Figure 3 retains the same qualitative cases against ReGenNet.

E5.justification: Both versions report numerical estimates with ± uncertainties, and the new R2R rows follow that practice. V2 adds no run counts, seeds, uncertainty definitions, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds seven R2R metrics per dataset, including FID 2.795±0.062 on InterHuman and 0.063±0.003 on InterX. R2R becomes the second-best FID method on both benchmarks. All pre-existing numerical entries in Tables 2-6 and the qualitative examples are unchanged.

T1.justification: The MeanFlow definition, loss and CFG equations, and VAE objective retain their mathematical content. V1's displayed single-step sampling equation is removed from Section 3, but the equivalent inference rule remains in Section 4.3; this is not a substantive theoretical removal.

C1.justification: The abstract lowers the headline FID improvement from 'over 40%' to 'about 30%'. The core contributions and state-of-the-art claims remain, while the introduction inconsistently retains 'over 40%'.

C2.justification: The explanations involving contextual drift, reactor history, compression versus fidelity, and online versus offline performance retain their meaning. The limitations concerning elastic delay handling and post-hoc classifier guidance are unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the statement that code is available in the supplementary with an explicit URL described as the official public implementation. Existing architecture, hyperparameter, training-budget, and hardware disclosures are retained. Repository availability was not independently verified.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Ready-to-React and Diff9D. Section 2 acknowledges R2R's full-history encoding while identifying its 50-step inference as an efficiency limitation, modestly refining the positioning against prior online methods.

P1.justification: V2 selectively condenses the preliminary explanation, CNN-VAE description, implementation details, and quantitative discussion, and adds acknowledgements. The main section organization and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains R2R rows and revised ranking emphasis. The unchanged Figure 3 moves from page 8 to page 7, and the ablation tables and surrounding text are rearranged. All three figure images are retained unchanged.

improvement.justification: Adding the stronger R2R baseline makes the central online comparison more informative while retaining ARMFlow's advantage, and the explicit implementation link improves reproducibility information. These limited gains are tempered by inconsistent claims: the introduction retains 'over 40%', and Section 5.1 reports a 28% InterHuman improvement although Table 2 gives approximately 22.1% using R2R's FID as the denominator.
